Publication Title	Comparative gene expression analysis in mouse models for multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease and stroke for identifying commonly regulated and disease-specific gene changes.
Publication Status
Publication Status Term Source REF
Experiment Description	Three mouse models of human central nervous system pathologies were selected for analyzing gene expression changes compared to wild type normal brain. The selected models are: TgAPP23 for Alzheimerï¾s disease (see Sturchler-Pierrat, C.,  Abramowski, D., Duke, M., Wiederhold, K.H., Mistl, C., Rothacher, S., Ledermann, B., B?rki, K., Frey, P., Paganetti, P.A., Waridel, C., Calhoun, M.E., Jucker, M., Probst, A., Staufenbiel, M. and Sommer, B. (1997) Two amyloid precursor protein transgenic mouse models with Alzheimer disease-like pathology. PNAS 94, 13287-13292), Tg6074 for multiple sclerosis (see Akassoglou K, Bauer J, Kassiotis G, Pasparakis M, Lassmann H, Kollias G and Probert L. (1998). Oligodendrocyte apoptosis and primary demyelination induced by local TNF/p55TNF receptor signaling in the central nervous system of transgenic mice: models for multiple sclerosis with primary oligodendrogliopathy. Am J Pathol. 153, 801-813) and permanent mid-cerebral artery occlusion for stroke (see Welsh, F.A., Sakamoto, T., McKee, A.E. and Sims, R.E. (1987) Effect of lactacidosis on pyridine nucleotide stability during ischemia in mouse brain. J Neurochem. 49, 846-851). Trangenic mice were grown to appropriate age, so that they would manifest the symptoms of disease or disease was induced by a surgical procedure to adult mice. Mice were sacrificed and half brains were removed at selected time points after disease onset for RNA extraction and subsequent array hybridization.
Protocol Name	P-MTAB-13	P-MTAB-14	P-MTAB-15	P-MTAB-17	P-MTAB-18	P-MTAB-19
Protocol Type	dissect	nucleic_acid_extraction	labeling	hybridization	feature_extraction	bioassay_data_transformation
Protocol Description	Two transgenic mouse lines were used as models for Alzheimer's disease and for chronic progressive multiple sclerosis, the TgAPP23 (kindly provided by Dr. M. Staufenbiel Novartis Pharma Ltd., Nervous Systems Research, Basel, Switzerland, described in Sturchler-Pierrat et al, 1997 ) and Tg6074 (previously described in Akassoglou et al, 1998), respectively. As a model for stroke, we used the permanent mid-cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model (Taoufik et al, 2007). Additionally, some validation studies were performed on samples derived from mice developing experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) induced after MOG35-55 immunization; the procedure for MOG-EAE induction is described elsewhere (Tseveleki et al, 2004). As controls, wild type littermates for each experimental animal were sacrificed at matching time points for each disease. All of the mice used were maintained in the animal facility of Hellenic Pasteur Institute under specific pathogen free conditions and all the experimental procedures conformed to the national and European guidelines for animal experimentation. Animals were used at the ages indicated for the TgAPP23 and the Tg6074 and between 6-8 weeks of age for the MCAO and EAE models. Total RNA was isolated from a rostro-caudal section of the whole mouse brain, using a half brain section for RNA extraction. 	Total RNA was isolated from a rostro-caudal section of the whole mouse brain, using a half brain section for RNA extraction. Briefly the tissue was snap frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -70oC. Without defrosting the sample was homogenized in Trizol reagent (Invitrogen) using a Ultra turrax T25 (Janke and Kunkel) tissue homogenizer and briefly sonicated using an Ultrasonic homogenizer (Cole and Parmer) sonicator. RNA was extracted according to manufacturer's instructions. Total RNA purity and concentration was determined prior to labeling and hybridization using the microfluidics-based platform 2100 Bioanalyzer (Agilent Technologies) and the RNA 6000 Nano LabChip kit. The universal reference RNA used as a control in all hybridizations (Stratagene) was total RNA isolated from various cell lines.	Detailed cDNA target preparation and hybridization protocols are available at http://compbio.dfci.harvard.edu/protocols.html. Briefly, cDNA was synthesized at 42ï¾ºC using 10?g of total RNA, 6?g random hexanucleotide primers, 200 units of SuperScript II (Invitrogen) reverse transcriptase in 1? first strand synthesis buffer containing 10mM DTT, 25mM dATP, 25mMdCTP, 25mM dGTP, 15mM dTTP, 10mM amino allyl-dUTP (Sigma). Following cDNA synthesis RNA was hydrolyzed for 15min at 65 0C with 200mM NaOH and 100mM EDTA. Unincorporated amino allyl-dUTP was removed through chromatography on QIAquick columns (Qiagen). Columns were washed with 5mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 8.5). Following lyophilization, the cDNA was resuspended in 4.5?l sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) buffer (pH 9.0), mixed with Cy3 or Cy5 NHS-ester (Amersham Biosciences) and incubated at ambient temperature for 1 hour. cDNA with incorporated Cy3 or Cy5 was purified using QIAquick columns, combined and lyophilized. 	TIGR cDNA microarray fabrication, RNA labeling and hybridization Microarrays were constructed using the National Institute of Aging (NIA) 15K and Trans-NIH Brain Molecular Anatomy Project (BMAP) mouse cDNA clone sets, containing a total of ~27,000 clones representing 19,263 unique transcripts. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplicons were prepared for printing as described previously (Hegde et al, 2000, Biotechniques). Following amplification and purification, amplicons were resuspended at 100-200nM in 50% DMSO and printed onto UltraGAPs aminosilane coated slides (Corning, Corning, NY) using an Intelligent Automation System (IAS) arrayer (Cambridge, MA). After printing, DNA was cross-linked to the slides by UV irradiation at 120mJ using a Stratalinker (Stratagene) and stored in a desiccated chamber until use.Detailed cDNA target preparation and hybridization protocols are available at http://pga.tigr.org/protocols.shtml. Briefly, cDNA was synthesized at 420C using 10ï¾µg of total RNA, 6ï¾µg random hexanucleotide primers, 200 units of SuperScript II (Invitrogen) reverse transcriptase in 1x first strand synthesis buffer containing 10mM DTT, 25mM dATP, 25mMdCTP, 25mM dGTP, 15mM dTTP, 10mM amino allyl-dUTP (Sigma). Following cDNA synthesis RNA was hydrolyzed for 15min at 65 0C with 200mM NaOH and 100mM EDTA. Unincorporated amino allyl-dUTP was removed through chromatography on QIAquick columns (Qiagen). Columns were washed with 5mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 8.5). Following lyophilization, the cDNA was resuspended in 4.5ï¾µl sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) buffer (pH 9.0), mixed with Cy3 or Cy5 NHS-ester (Amersham Biosciences) and incubated at ambient temperature for 1 hour. cDNA with incorporated Cy3 or Cy5 was purified using QIAquick columns, combined and lyophilized. Slides were prehybridized in 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 5%SSC, 0.1% SDS for 40 minutes at 420C, after which slides were washed and dried. Cy3 and Cy5 labeled cDNA was resuspended in 30ï¾µl of 50% formamide, 5xSSC, 0.1%SDS containing 0.5ï¾µg mouse Cot-1 DNA (Gibco BRL), 1ï¾µg poly-dA and hybridized to the microarray at 420C for 16 hours under glas coverslips. Following hybridization, slides were washed for 4 minutes at 420C in solution containing 2xSSC, 0.2% SDS followed by a 4 minute wash in 0.2xSSC, 0.1% SDS and a 2.5 minute wash in 0.05xSSC at ambient temperature. All samples were hybridized with dye-reversal replicates and duplicate hybridizations of randomly selected samples were performed.	Images were analyzed with the application TIGR Spotfinder, version 2	Data normalization was performed using the TIGR MIDAS software (http://www.tigr.org/software/tm4). All signal intensities from flip-dye hybridization pairs were processed in MIDAS using a locally weighted scatterplot smoothing regression (LOWESS) algorithm with the smoothing parameter set to 0.33, followed by standard deviation regularization across array-grids and flip-dye consistency checking to keep data with the range of ï¾±2.0 SD. Data from the reverse-dye replicates as well as both direct and indirect comparisons were used to compute comparisons of experimental to control pools. For indirect comparisons through the reference RNA, the log2(ratio) of comparisons between experimental samples was inferred for each gene using the relationship: log2 (A/B) ? log2 (A/R1) ï¾ log2 (B/R2), where A and B are the experimental samples being compared and R represents the expression level measured for the reference RNA.
